title: Keep the first release finishable
subtitle: Validate the idea with one small, complete workflow.
concept: Build only enough to complete the initial scenario. Record other ideas for later.
intuition: Build a usable bicycle before deciding whether it needs a basket; do not commission an entire transport system at once.
objectives: List the essential features forming one complete workflow.
Attach an immediate check to each small change.

body.title: Draw the smallest complete workflow
body.text: For the study list: add a plan, see it, complete or delete it, then find it next time. Display and persistence are essential. Accounts, rankings, reminders and cross-device synchronization are deferred deliberately.

body.title: Separate now from later
body.text: Use two lists: required now and consider later. Ask of each requirement: without it, can the user still complete this scenario? If yes, defer it. Scope can change, but update the plan and acceptance criteria honestly.

body.title: Deliver one checkable change at a time
body.text: First show an empty list, then add items, then completion, then persistence. Each task needs a check. A single finish-the-site task postpones discovering unsuitable data or storage design. Small steps reveal errors early, not merely shorten prompts.

formalDefinition.text: Build only enough to complete the initial scenario. Record other ideas for later.
conditions: For small personal learning projects. In shared repositories, follow the team's conventions.
This method produces checkable evidence; it cannot guarantee arbitrary AI output is correct.

workflow: List the essential features forming one complete workflow.
Defer ideas unnecessary for that workflow.
Attach an immediate check to each small change.

workedExamples.title: Deciding about login
workedExamples.problem: Does a personal single-browser first release need login?
steps: Complete the scenario with local storage and state its limits.
workedExamples.answer: No login initially. Data stays in this browser and does not synchronize to other devices. If synchronization becomes necessary, redesign accounts and storage then.

workedExamples.title: Split a large task
workedExamples.problem: How would you divide finish the study list?
steps: Display the page and empty state first.
Add creation, completion and deletion, checking each action.
Then add persistence and backup, checking refresh and restoration.
workedExamples.answer: Task 1: empty list. Task 2: add nonblank plans and reject whitespace. Task 3: toggle and delete by ID. Task 4: refresh persistence and JSON backup. Verify each separately and fix failures before continuing.

commonMistakes.claim: More features make a better first release.
commonMistakes.correction: First establish that one workflow is useful; extras add delay and ambiguity.
Prefer verifiable behaviors; one small behavior may touch several files.

practice.problem: Which comes first: reminders, rankings or adding plans?
practice.answer: Adding plans. The other two are not essential to a personal list.
solution: Make recording and retrieval work first.
Keep other ideas on the later list.

practice.problem: How should you explain the absence of cloud synchronization?
practice.hint: State what happens on another device.
practice.answer: Data is stored only in this browser. Changing devices or clearing storage will not restore it automatically; download a backup.
solution: Put limitations in user-facing instructions, not just the development plan.

practice.problem: Turn finish the page into one small task.
practice.hint: Choose behavior you can verify by clicking.
practice.answer: Submitting a nonblank title adds an item; whitespace-only input gives a message without adding anything.

practice.problem: What if multiuser synchronization becomes mandatory midway?
practice.hint: It changes data location and permissions.
practice.answer: Revisit the plan, confirm sharing and permissions, rewrite scope and acceptance criteria, then estimate the new tasks.
solution: Do not pretend a personal-list design only needs another button.

learningCheck.question: Which belongs in the first release?
choices: A personal list with automatic payments
Add, complete, delete and save locally
feedback: Payments add another business problem and risks.
This completes the original scenario with clear scope.
Several new scenarios make the first release harder to finish.

interactiveVisual.prediction: Four tempting additions are suggested. Which deserve inclusion now?

steps.question: The agent proposes accounts, but only you use the app.
choices: Defer them and explain local-storage limits
feedback: Scope stays clear and the user understands its limits.
This breaks finding plans on a later day.

steps.question: Refreshing loses the list.
choices: Fix this gap in the first release
feedback: Persistence is part of the current scenario.
New features cannot repair a broken core workflow.
A title change does not prevent data loss.

steps.question: One change includes creation, login and payments. How should it be adjusted?
choices: Use a longer prompt for everything
Split it and verify creation first
feedback: A longer description does not reduce change scope.
Smaller changes are easier to understand and verify.
